title: Sequoia Lend - Dedicated capacity discovery
summary: Initial dedicated capacity discovery for latency-sensitive lending products. Customer needs reserved GPUs, strict isolation and data residency, burst capacity for peak loan processing, and clear SLAs. Security and SSO/KMS were high priority; next steps include benchmark run, pricing worksheet, and security packet share.
action_items: Alex Mercer - Share Dedicated pricing worksheet and burst policy doc (due: 2026-11-27)
Priya Shah - Run sample benchmark plan and propose node sizing (due: 2026-12-01)
Daniel Kim - Share expected QPS and peak windows + existing infra diagram (due: 2026-11-30)
next_steps: Redwood to run 48-hour benchmark with their sample payload (Priya)
Send security packet & SOC2 report link (Alex)
Follow-up demo on Dedicated console and routing policies next week
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-24
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Mercer (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Daniel Kim (CTO), Rina Patel (Head of ML), Marcus Lee (Infra)

[00:00] Alex Mercer: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick intros and then we'll jump in. I'm Alex, I'm the AE, Priya is our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Daniel Kim: Hi all, Daniel here, CTO at Sequoia Lend. Rina and Marcus are on as well. trying to move on a dedicated inference plan for our credit decisioning pipelines.
[00:22] Rina Patel: hi, yeah we're evaluating options, we need reserved GPUs for compliance and predictable throughput.
[00:30] Priya Shah: great, thanks. to set expectations, we'd like to understand your workload patterns, latency targets, and any isolation/regulatory requirements so we can size dedicated pools.
[00:41] Marcus Lee: sure. quick overview — our latency SLO on the realtime scoring path is p95 < 220ms for single-turn prompts, with bursts during business hours up to 4x baseline qps. we currently use a mixed fleet on prem and cloud kubernetes for model orchestration.
[00:58] Alex Mercer: good context. is the 220ms p95 token-level or end-to-end infer latency including network?
[01:05] Marcus Lee: that's end-to-end from our app to response, so network adds ~30-40ms. so inference target is more like 180ms.
[01:13] Priya Shah: okay that helps. for Dedicated capacity we typically recommend reserving a baseline GPU pool sized for steady qps and a burst pool or autoscaler for peaks. do you have estimates of baseline qps and peak qps numbers?
[01:28] Rina Patel: baseline ~60 qps, peak around 240 qps for 2-3 hour windows. average prompt length is ~220 tokens, typical models are 7B-13B open models, some quantized.
[01:42] Alex Mercer: good. the 4x burst factor aligns with options where you reserve X GPUs for baseline and configure burst policy to use extra capacity or preemptible resources. question on isolation — are you looking for tenant isolation at network level only or full hardware isolation?
[01:57] Daniel Kim: full isolation if possible. compliance is strict for some of our lenders, they want dedicated GPU pools and VPC peering or private deployment. SOC2 is table stakes.
[02:06] Priya Shah: we support Dedicated with dedicated GPU pools and VPC peering, plus Redwood Private for on-prem or air-gapped. Dedicated gives logical isolation and dedicated nodes; Private gives you customer-managed control plane. which direction are you leaning?
[02:19] Rina Patel: we want Redwood Dedicated to start for pace and manageability, but may evaluate Private for certain high-risk customers. need to confirm data residency and KMS integration though.
[02:30] Marcus Lee: KMS is required, HSM if possible. Also, we need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[02:36] Alex Mercer: yes we can integrate with customer KMS and forward audit logs. I'll share the security pack with details. link: https://redwood.ai/security-pack (note: auto transcript sometimes mangles links).
[02:49] Daniel Kim: cool. on the cost side — our finance team will ask about unit costs at baseline vs burst, and any overage caps.
[02:58] Priya Shah: we'll send a pricing worksheet that breaks down per-token and per-hour GPU amortized cost for baseline and burst, plus an example for continuous batching and KV cache savings.
[03:08] Rina Patel: KV cache — we frequently have identical prefixes in prompts for scoring, so caching could be big. do you support prefix/KV cache on Dedicated?
[03:16] Priya Shah: yes, Dedicated supports prefix and KV cache. we can configure hot-prefix cache to reduce redundant compute; that can cut effective cost significantly for your workload. we'll include expected token-level reductions in the benchmark.
[03:26] Marcus Lee: about autoscaling — how fast can Dedicated scale up? we can't tolerate cold-start latency spikes that blow past SLOs.
[03:34] Priya Shah: autoscaling in Dedicated is configurable; you can have warm standbys and incremental node provisioning. warm standby nodes keep KV caches hot; we recommend a mix of reserved baseline + warm buffer + burst on demand for your pattern. typical scale-up times vary by infra (10-60s for starting a new process), but with warm buffers you avoid token-level latency cliffs.
[03:51] Daniel Kim: if warm nodes exist, does that increase cost similar to reserved nodes?
[03:55] Alex Mercer: yes warm nodes are billed like reserved capacity, but you can tune the size of the warm pool to balance cost vs risk. we'll model that in the spreadsheet.
[04:03] Rina Patel: on model variants — we plan to fallback to smaller quantized models for non-critical paths. do you handle automatic fallback policies?
[04:11] Priya Shah: Redwood supports routing policies where you can set primary -> fallback models with automatic failover and also region fallback. that helps maintain availability while trading down for cost.
[04:20] Marcus Lee: great. any constraints around our existing infra? we use AWS us-east-2 for most workloads; can Dedicated be deployed in specific cloud regions and peered to our VPC?
[04:30] Alex Mercer: yes Dedicated regions can be selected and we support VPC peering; Private on-prem would be separate. we'll note region for the proposal.
[04:36] Daniel Kim: security questions — do you have SOC2 and ISO certs? and how granular is RBAC and SSO?
[04:42] Alex Mercer: SOC2 Type II available, ISO is in progress. RBAC with role scoping and SSO via SAML/OIDC are supported. I'll attach SOC2 and the SSO integration guide.
[04:52] Rina Patel: perfect. for benchmarks — we want Redwood to run tests using our sample payload and our 13B quantized model variant. can you run a 48-hour test that simulates business-hour bursts?
[05:01] Priya Shah: yes, we can. we'll need your payload, a test script and expected QPS windows. propose we run it next week, capture latency percentiles and token costs, and return a benchmark report.
[05:12] Daniel Kim: we'll provide that. timeline wise, pilot in early January if results look good.
[05:19] Alex Mercer: sounds reasonable. any procurement constraints we should know about? PO process, legal timelines?
[05:24] Marcus Lee: procurement typically needs vendor security questionnaire and master services agreement review — two to three weeks. pricing approvals take another week.
[05:32] Alex Mercer: ok we'll prioritize the security docs and draft SOW.
[05:36] Rina Patel: one more — are there GPU types you recommend for 13B quantized models? we have experience with A10G and A100.
[05:44] Priya Shah: for 13B quantized, A10G or H100 with appropriate kernel options both work. A10G gives good cost efficiency; H100 provides headroom for larger context sizes and very low latency. we'll include recommendations and expected throughput in the sizing doc.
[05:58] Daniel Kim: any concern about model compilation or kernel selection? we saw some runtimes struggle on long sequences.
[06:04] Priya Shah: Redwood runtime does compilation and kernel selection per model and sequence profile. for your 220-token average we'll pick kernels optimized for that distribution; we'll also test with your longer tails during the benchmark.
[06:15] Alex Mercer: good — to recap, we'll: 1) send security pack and SOC2, 2) share pricing worksheet and burst policy examples, 3) Priya will run a benchmark plan once Sequoia shares payload and qps windows, 4) schedule follow-up demo focused on Dedicated console and routing/rollout policies.
[06:36] Marcus Lee: yep that covers it.
[06:39] Daniel Kim: thanks folks. one tiny nit — do you support forwarding logs to Splunk?
[06:44] Alex Mercer: yes audit logs and request traces can be forwarded to common SIEMs including Splunk; will add config notes.
[06:51] Rina Patel: ok thanks. looking forward to the benchmark results.
[06:55] Priya Shah: we'll get started. thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
